answers.explanation:
1. [Question 1: Is it possible to create a solution that the existing explorer could not produce with another deterministic generator?]
   -> **It is possible.** If the existing generator only explored orbit $O_1$, the impossible solutions can be derived 100% deterministically by building an 'extended deterministic generator (Generator Family)' that includes Rotation Shift or Complement Flip as a deterministic symmetry conversion operator.

2. [Question 2: Are there solutions that absolutely cannot be generated by any deterministic generator?]
   -> **Exists.** An independent orbit $\text{Orbit}(G_B)$ that is completely separate from the set of orbits $\text{Orbit}(G_A)$ created by a specific deterministic solver $G_A$ exists in the solution space. Therefore, from the perspective of any single deterministic solver that cannot cover all orbits in the solution space, there is always an isolated true solution (Orbit-Isolated Solution) that can never be reached by its algorithm rules.
